headline: The Workspace area — the app's home for projects, chat panels, knowledge graph and access control — has seven tickets all marked released, of which two are backed by code the analysis could read and five could not be confirmed either way from the files examined.
what_is_there: The analysis found a working knowledge-graph visualisation (an interactive force-directed graph with search, legend and tooltips) and a complete chat-history backend supporting saved conversations, search, rename, delete and pinning — the things a history sidebar needs. It also saw the main application shell wiring in a workspace tab and a chat tab, described in the code as the app's home for project management.
what_is_unclear: Five tickets — project create/rename/delete/duplicate, multi-tab chat sessions, the folder picker for AI-edit targets, workspace member management with roles, and trash with restore — could not be settled because the actual workspace and chat tab screens were not among the files the analysis looked at. For the two confirmed items, the backend and rendering were seen but the on-screen components were inferred rather than directly observed.
suggested_action: Ask the team to point the next review pass at the workspace and chat tab screens, and at wherever membership and permissions live, so the five unconfirmed tickets can be checked directly.
